info.title: My TV Channel — Agent API
info.summary: Create and run 24/7 linear HLS TV channels programmatically.
info.description:
Create and run 24/7 linear TV channels — the kind that just play, with no menu to browse.
Import videos, and the service transcodes them, builds a continuous schedule, and streams
the result at `https://{handle}.my-tv-channel.com` and in the iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, macOS,
Android, Fire TV and Roku apps.

## Before you start

- **Every response uses the same envelope:** `{"success": true, "data": ...}` or
  `{"success": false, "error": "...", "code": N}`. There is exactly one exception, and it
  is called out on the operation: `GET /channels/schedule.php` returns `data` as a bare
  **array**.
- **Authentication is an API key**, `Authorization: Bearer mytv_sk_...`, created by a
  signed-in human at <https://my-tv-channel.com/agent-keys/> or in the app under
  Profile → Agent Access. An active subscription on any tier is required, and the key
  inherits the owner's tier limits. **An agent cannot mint its own key, by design** — if
  you do not have one, ask the owner for one.
- **Rate limit:** 1,000 requests/hour per key. Exceeding it returns `429` with
  `Retry-After`; honour it rather than spinning.
- **Start with `GET /users/status.php`.** It returns the tier, the real quota numbers for
  this account, every channel, and for each one exactly what it still needs before it can
  go live. Agents that skip this step guess, and guessing is expensive.

## The two things that catch everyone

1. **Weights only reach the air when the schedule is generated.** A channel builds its
   schedule the instant it crosses the launch threshold, from the weights present at that
   moment. Weights set afterwards are stored faithfully, reported back correctly, and do
   not change what is broadcasting. Either set each asset's weight as soon as it reports
   `ready`, or call `POST /schedule/regenerate.php` when you are done.
2. **You cannot upload a local file over MCP**, because tool arguments are JSON and there
   is no multipart channel. `POST /assets/import-url.php` is therefore the ingestion path
   for an agent. `POST /assets/upload.php` exists for clients that can post multipart.

## Going live

A channel launches **automatically** once it has ≥ 4 ready assets **and** ≥ 15 minutes of
content with weight > 0. Transcoding is the slow step. Poll `GET /assets/status.php` for
`summary.meetsLaunchRequirements`, then `GET /channels/get.php` until `scheduleStatus` is
`active`, then report the watch URL to the owner.

servers.description: Production (legacy host, still live — prefer the canonical one)

get.summary: Who am I — tier, limits, quotas, channels and launch gaps
get.description:
**The right first call.** Returns the owner's subscription tier and the real limits
for this account, upload and streaming quota used vs remaining over a rolling 7-day
window, and every channel with its `launchGaps` — a human-readable list of what each
channel still needs, e.g. `"needs 2 more ready asset(s)"`.

Do not hardcode tier limits from documentation; read them from here. Quota is measured
in seconds for upload and minutes for streaming.

Returns the device tag used to prove YouTube ownership, in the form
`MyTVChannelApp#<device_id>`. The owner pastes this exact string into a video's
description or tags on YouTube; only the uploader can do that, which is the proof.

See `POST /assets/import-youtube.php`. **Relay the string verbatim** — it is matched
exactly.

200.description: The ownership tag for this account

get.description: A narrower view of the quota already included in `GET /users/status.php`. Prefer that call unless you specifically only want quota.
Check before calling `create_channel`. The handle becomes the subdomain, so it is permanent in practice — archiving a channel keeps its handle reserved.

post.description:
Creates a channel. It starts private and off air; it goes live by itself once the
launch requirements are met.

`is_public: true` lists it in Discover and is available on **every** tier, including
Starter. Never tell an owner to upgrade for public listing — an earlier version of the
documentation said Creator+ was required and that was wrong.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Pass `me` to restrict the list to channels owned by the authenticated account.

get.summary: One channel, including whether it is on air
get.description:
**This is the call that tells you whether a channel is broadcasting.** Poll
`scheduleStatus` (also returned as `schedule_status`) until it reads `active`, then
report `watchUrl` to the owner.

put.description:
**The channel id goes in the query string as `?id=N`**, not in the body. This is the
opposite of `PUT /assets/update.php`, where the id goes in the body as `asset_id`. The
inconsistency is real; both are documented here so you do not have to find out.

Only allowlisted fields are accepted; anything else is ignored rather than erroring.

post.summary: Take a channel off air (archive, not destroy)
post.description:
Takes the channel off air and removes it from every listing. **Not destructive in the
irreversible sense:** the handle stays reserved and the assets are retained.

Idempotent — safe to retry. Returns `409` if transcodes are still running for the
channel; wait for them or retry.

409.description: Transcodes are still running for this channel

get.description:
Returns the electronic programme guide — what is playing and what is next.

**Two things are unlike every other endpoint here.** This one needs **no
authentication**, because an EPG is public; and its `data` is a **bare array**, not an
object. If you wrote a generic response handler that reaches into `data.something`, it
will break precisely here.

post.description:
Posts a video file directly. **An MCP client cannot call this** — tool arguments are
JSON and there is no multipart channel. Use `POST /assets/import-url.php` instead, or
have the owner upload through the app.

Accepted: MP4, MOV, M4V, MPEG, AVI. Duration is charged against the rolling 7-day
upload quota. The asset lands in `pending` and follows
`pending → transcoding → ready`.

413.description: Body too large. If you see an HTML error page rather than the JSON envelope here, it came from the web server rather than the application.

post.summary: Import a video from a public URL
post.description:
**The main way an agent adds content.** The server fetches the file, so you do not
download it yourself.

The URL must be a **direct, public, unauthenticated** media link — `mp4`, `mov`,
`m4v`, `mpeg`, `mpg`, `avi`, or a **finite** `.m3u8` (VOD, not a live stream). Not a
web page, not something behind a login.

- Rejected with `400` immediately if it cannot be probed as video, so you get a clear
  error rather than a silent failure later.
- Quota is charged on the video's duration, checked at submit **and** re-verified
  against the real file after download — a source that misreports duration fails then.
- Maximum 20 queued imports at a time (`429` beyond that).
- Submitting the same URL to the same channel twice returns the original asset with
  `duplicate: true` instead of importing again, so retries are safe.

Returns immediately; the asset starts at `downloading`, then
`pending → transcoding → ready`. **Set `weight` here** rather than after the fact —
see the note on the schedule endpoints.

200.description: Import queued (or an existing asset, if this URL was already imported)

400.description: Not a direct media URL, or it could not be probed as video

429.description: More than 20 imports are already queued

post.summary: Import a YouTube video the owner proves they own
post.description:
Imports a YouTube video, but **only one the owner can prove they uploaded** — and you
cannot perform that proof for them:

1. Get the owner's tag from `GET /users/device.php`
   (`MyTVChannelApp#<device_id>`).
2. Ask them to paste that exact string into the video's **description or tags on
   YouTube**. Only the uploader can edit those; that is the proof.
3. Retry the import.

If the tag is missing you get `403` whose message **already contains the exact string
to paste — relay it verbatim**, do not paraphrase or reformat it.

Public, finished videos only: no live streams, no private or age-restricted videos, no
playlists or channel URLs. Capped at 10 imports per day. Same quota as upload.

Never try to import a video the owner did not upload. The check exists because a
channel built from other people's videos is a copyright problem for the owner.

403.description: Ownership not proved, or quota exceeded. When ownership is the cause, the `error` string contains the exact tag for the owner to publish — pass it through unchanged.

get.summary: List the videos on a channel
Poll transcoding, and find out when the channel can launch
get.description:
Each asset reports `uploadStatus` (`downloading → pending → transcoding → ready`) and
transcode progress. The `summary` object reports `meetsLaunchRequirements`, which is
what you actually want.

Poll every 30–60 seconds. Transcoding takes roughly real-time ÷ 4, depending on load
on the encoding farm. Give exactly one of `channel_id` or `asset_id`.

put.summary: Set a video's weight, title or tags
put.description:
**The asset id goes in the BODY as `asset_id`** — `?id=N` is also accepted, but the
body form is canonical. This is the opposite of `PUT /channels/update.php`, where the
id goes in the query string.

`weight` (0–10, default 5) controls how often the video plays. `0` removes it from
scheduling entirely without deleting it.

**Set the weight as soon as the asset reports `ready`, not after all imports finish.**
The channel auto-launches the instant it crosses the launch threshold and builds its
schedule from the weights that exist at that moment. On a measured run, a channel went
live 16 seconds after the final transcode and weights set 20 seconds later had zero
effect — a weight-3 asset got identical airtime to a weight-9 one. If the channel is
already live, follow this with `POST /schedule/regenerate.php`.

For an ordered mini-series, tag assets `seqXX01`, `seqXX02`, … (XX = any two letters).
They always play in order, and only the `01` episode enters the random draw.

post.description:
Stops the asset being scheduled, cancels any running transcode, and auto-regenerates
the schedule. **Soft delete** — the file survives a grace period. Idempotent.

Deletes are reversible by design, so prefer cleaning up after yourself to leaving
debris. Never delete content you did not create in this session unless the owner asked.

post.summary: Rebuild the schedule now, with the current weights
post.description:
**Call this after changing weights on a channel that is already live**, or the change
will not air until the hourly cron picks it up.

Destructive in the sense that it replaces what was going to air — but not
irreversible; it rebuilds from current state. Manual rows placed by
`POST /schedule/batch-insert.php` survive regeneration.

Throttled to **one call per channel per 5 minutes**. On `429`, honour `Retry-After`;
do not spin.

post.summary: Place specific assets in the schedule manually (Pro tier and above)
post.description: Manual placement. Requires **Pro tier or above** — check `tier` from `GET /users/status.php` first and tell the owner an upgrade is needed rather than retrying into `403`. Rows placed this way survive schedule regeneration.

**Always call this before `PUT /schedule/rules.php`.** It takes exactly the payload
that `rules.php` accepts, **saves nothing**, and returns
`{valid, errors[], warnings[], preview[]}` including a simulated 24-hour grid.

Deliberately **not tier-gated**, so you can preview a ruleset on any plan — including
one the owner could not yet commit.

200.description: Validation result and a simulated 24-hour grid

get.summary: The current ruleset for a channel

put.summary: Replace the whole ruleset (Pro tier and above)
put.description:
**This REPLACES the entire ruleset**, it does not merge. Read the current rules first
if you intend to add one, and always run `POST /schedule/validate.php` on the payload
before committing it.

Requires **Pro tier or above**. Rules are durable intent: the scheduler re-honours
them every time it rebuilds, so you compile the owner's wishes once rather than
babysitting the grid.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key, `Authorization: Bearer mytv_sk_...`. Created by a signed-in human at
<https://my-tv-channel.com/agent-keys/> or in the app under Profile → Agent Access.
Requires an active subscription on any tier; the key inherits the owner's tier limits.

Key management — creating and revoking — is deliberately impossible with an API key,
so an agent holding one cannot escalate to issuing more. **Never ask the owner for
their Apple password or app login.** The key is all you need.

error.description: Human-readable. For the YouTube ownership failure this string contains the exact tag the owner must publish — relay it verbatim.

Handle.description: 3–63 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Becomes the channel's subdomain — `https://{handle}.my-tv-channel.com` — so treat it as permanent.

Weight.description: How often the video plays, relative to the others. `0` excludes it from scheduling without deleting it. Do not set everything to 10 — the *differences* between weights are what shape a channel.

channel_type.description: `location` requires a `location` object. `thematic` is the usual choice.

is_public.description: List the channel in Discover. **Available on every tier**, including Starter.

schedule_status.description: Snake-case alias of `scheduleStatus`; both are returned.

launchGaps.description: What this channel still needs before it can go live, in plain language. Empty once the requirements are met.

duplicate.description: Present and true when this URL had already been imported to this channel, in which case the original asset is returned rather than a new import being started.

timezone.description: IANA name, e.g. `Europe/Paris`. **Set this** — rule times are wall clock in the channel timezone, and omitting it means UTC, which is almost never what the owner meant. `schedule_timezone` is also accepted.

Rule.description:
A `time_slot` puts something on at a time. A `daypart_weight` changes how likely
something is during a window.

**Slots start ON-OR-AFTER their time.** The programme running into a slot is never cut
short, so an 18:00 slot may actually begin at 18:02. That is deliberate — a linear
channel must not chop a video in half to hit a clock time. Do not report it as a fault.

end_time.description: On a `time_slot`, this makes it a **block**: it keeps drawing from the selector until this time. Without it you get a single programme, not a morning of cartoons.

days_mask.description: Bitmask — bit0=Mon, bit1=Tue … bit6=Sun. `127` = every day, `31` = Mon–Fri, `96` = weekend.

selector_value.description: An asset id, a tag string, or — for `playlist` — an array of asset ids, which play in order.

weight_multiplier.description: `daypart_weight` only. `0` removes matching assets from that window entirely.

limits.description: The real limits for this account. Read them here rather than hardcoding.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request or a rejected value

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key

NotFound.description: No such resource, or it does not belong to this account

QuotaExceeded.description: Weekly quota exceeded. The message reports the remaining allowance. Tell the owner a plan upgrade is needed rather than retrying into repeated 403s.

TierRequired.description: This operation needs a higher subscription tier. Check `tier` from `GET /users/status.php` before calling rather than discovering it here.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit or throttle exceeded — 1,000 requests/hour per key, and separately one schedule regeneration per channel per 5 minutes. Honour `Retry-After`; do not spin.
